claim: The paper's statement that its throughput gain extends to larger mixture-of-experts models (Qwen3-235B-A22B, DeepSeek-V3 and Kimi-K2.6) is not established, because those speedups were measured on copies of the models with random weights, whose routers do not send tokens to the experts the trained models would choose, and the inter-node traffic that the speedup comes from depends on exactly those routing choices.
evidence: Section 5.4 (page 9) reports 1.15x, 1.18x and 1.05x throughput on Qwen3-235B-A22B, DeepSeek-V3 and Kimi-K2.6 under the heading "The implementation and throughput gain extends to larger MoE architectures", and states that "these tests use full-sized models with random weights and report throughput improvements only." The traffic these speedups come from depends on routing: Appendix F.1 (page 24) computes it from the trained Qwen3-30B-A3B's routing, "routed transfers reach 2.73 remote nodes per token on average", and says the estimates "remain fixed for a given configuration, topology and routing trace." A randomly initialised router produces a different routing trace, so the larger-model runs measure neither the accuracy cost of the compression on those models nor the traffic, and hence the speedup, under their real routing.
